title: Multi-omics models guide experimental validation of flowering-time genes
summary: Researchers trained models on genomic, transcriptomic and methylomic data for Arabidopsis traits and used feature interpretation to select flowering-time gene candidates. The preprint reports nine experimentally validated genes inferred to contribute to flowering time, tested using mutant phenotypes. Random-forest and ridge-regression models were used, so do not assign every gene to the random forest alone. Count one study, not nine discoveries. This draft follows the primary 2023 preprint version; the journal paper appeared in 2024.
ai_technology: Random-forest models; ridge regression; multi-omics integration
organization: DOE Great Lakes Bioenergy Research Center, Michigan State University; Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences

source_review.scope: Primary bioRxiv v1 full text, posted-date line, abstract, methods and author affiliations.

evidence.tested: The preprint reports experimental validation of nine flowering-time gene candidates using single- and/or double-mutant phenotypes.
evidence.unknown: Individual candidate-selection routes are not all attributed to one model; the result is from a preprint version and does not establish independent replication.
evidence.ai_role: Random-forest and ridge-regression models used multi-omics data to predict plant traits and identify features associated with flowering-time predictions.
